correctness.rationale: For fixed |z|<1, the binomial series converges uniformly in w, and the weighted input is in L1 by Cauchy–Schwarz. Angular orthogonality and the normalized beta integral give the two orthogonal mode systems. Parseval at each radius and integration then give ||Tf||² as the sum of s_n² times the squared normalized input coefficients, with maximal L2 domain containing all finite mode sums and the orthogonal complement. The gamma ratio yields the power c-L and a positive leading constant, proving the boundedness, compactness and p-summability tests. The consecutive ratio has crossing exactly at h_n. Rationalizing gives L-h_n=(a-b)²/(n+L+sqrt((n+L)²-(a-b)²)); this is strictly decreasing to zero for unequal weights and gives the escape constant for either maximizing index at a tie. At c=L, unequal weights give an increasing sequence approaching its limit strictly from below, so the Parseval sum has strictly positive norm deficit on every nonzero input. For equal weights the boundary positive multiplier is constant and left and right systems agree, hence a scaled orthogonal projection. Below that boundary the singular sequence decreases because each ratio is less than one; the proof's phrase 'decreasing below criticality' refers to that sequence, not to the numerical ratios as a function of n.
residual_risks: Outside compactness the listed modal coefficients are eigenvalues of the modulus on input modes, not a decreasing sequence of approximation numbers. No assertion about the absolute-value kernel follows.

The claim is a reusable complete classification, not just the boundedness line or selected examples.
